candidates.name: Early Marginal Spreading
candidates.idea: Adds an early quadratic plus steep quartic marginal-style penalty on planned load with live-time inflation and peak plus ramp plus signal plus low-capacity buffers to divert routes before saturation.
candidates.code: const F = road.freeSeconds; let V = road.liveSeconds; let L = road.load; if (L < 0) L = 0; let L2 = L * L; let L4 = L2 * L2; let peak = 0; if (road.hour > 6.5) { if (road.hour < 9.5) { peak = 1; } else { if (road.hour > 15.5) { if (road.hour < 19.5) { peak = 1; } } } } let cong = 0.9 * L2 + 1.6 * L4; if (peak > 0) cong = cong + 0.5 * L2; let bpr = F * (1 + cong); let base = F; if (V > F) base = V; let live = base * (1 + 0.35 * L2); if (peak > 0) live = live + base * 0.15 * L2; let cost = bpr; if (live > bpr) cost = live; if (road.isRamp > 0) cost = cost + F * 0.1 + F * 0.3 * L2; if (road.hasSignal > 0) cost = cost + F * 0.2 * L2; if (road.capacityPerHour < 800) cost = cost + F * 0.15 * L2; if (road.isFreeway > 0) cost = cost * 0.97; return cost;

candidates.name: Differentiated Marginal Tolls
candidates.idea: Adding type specific marginal externality tolls spreads selfish routing toward system optimum by protecting freeways and strongly penalizing ramp overloads while leaving surface streets as relief.
candidates.code:
const f = road.freeSeconds
const lv = road.liveSeconds
const q = road.load
const q2 = q * q
const q4 = q2 * q2
let priv = f * (1 + 0.45 * q4)
if (lv > priv) priv = lv
let toll = f * (0.25 * q2 + 0.65 * q4)
if (road.isRamp > 0) toll = f * (0.9 * q2 + 2.2 * q4)
else if (road.isFreeway > 0) toll = f * (0.5 * q2 + 1.5 * q4)
let mult = 1
if (road.hour > 6.5) if (road.hour < 9.5) mult = 1.3
if (road.hour > 15.5) if (road.hour < 19.5) mult = 1.3
return priv + mult * toll

candidates.name: Peak Reserving Toll
candidates.idea: Time-varying marginal toll with peak-centered reservation spreads early flow off freeways and ramps, peaks tolls during buildup, then relaxes after clearing while protecting low-capacity signal roads.

candidates.name: Tiered Early Overload Toll
candidates.idea: Tiered quadratic tolls spread planned load early by road type with peak and low-capacity multipliers plus a steep wall past 90 percent load to prevent queue spillover.
candidates.code: const f = road.freeSeconds; const lv = road.liveSeconds; let q = road.load; if (q < 0) q = 0; const q2 = q * q; const q4 = q2 * q2; let bpr = f * (1 + 0.45 * q4); let priv = bpr; if (lv > bpr) priv = lv; let a2 = 0.5; let a4 = 1.0; if (road.isRamp > 0) { a2 = 1.4; a4 = 3.0; } else { if (road.isFreeway > 0) { a2 = 0.8; a4 = 2.0; } else { if (road.hasSignal > 0) { a2 = 0.65; a4 = 1.3; } } } let mult = 1; if (road.hour > 6.5) { if (road.hour < 9.5) { mult = 1.4; } else { if (road.hour > 15.5) { if (road.hour < 19.5) { mult = 1.4; } } } } let cm = 1; if (road.capacityPerHour < 600) { cm = 1.4; } else { if (road.capacityPerHour < 1200) { cm = 1.15; } } let om = 0; if (q > 0.9) om = q - 0.9; let overload = om * om * 12; let toll = mult * cm * (a2 * q2 + a4 * q4) + overload * q2; return priv + f * toll;

candidates.name: Ramp Spillback Hierarchy
candidates.idea: Ramps get fixed plus convex spillback tolls, freeways stay cheap when empty but steep when full, and locals are protected so arterials absorb relief.
candidates.code: const f = road.freeSeconds; const lv = road.liveSeconds; let q = road.load; if (q < 0) q = 0; const q2 = q * q; const q4 = q2 * q2; const q6 = q4 * q2; let priv = f * (1 + 0.45 * q4); if (lv > priv) priv = lv; let peak = 0; if (road.hour > 6.5) { if (road.hour < 9.5) peak = 1; else { if (road.hour > 15.5) { if (road.hour < 19.5) peak = 1; } } } let toll = 0; if (road.isRamp > 0) { toll = f * (0.6 * q2 + 2.0 * q4 + 1.2 * q6) + f * 0.25 + 6 * q2 + 18 * q4; if (peak > 0) toll = toll * 1.5; } else { if (road.isFreeway > 0) { toll = f * (0.12 * q2 + 1.7 * q4 + 1.4 * q6); if (peak > 0) toll = toll * 1.45; if (q < 0.6) toll = toll * 0.7; } else { if (road.isArterial > 0) { toll = f * (0.18 * q2 + 0.7 * q4); if (road.hasSignal > 0) toll = toll + f * 0.25 * q2; if (peak > 0) toll = toll * 1.2; } else { toll = f * (0.35 * q2 + 1.0 * q4); if (road.hasSignal > 0) toll = toll + f * 0.3 * q2; if (road.capacityPerHour < 800) toll = toll + f * 0.4 * q2 + 4 * q2; if (peak > 0) toll = toll * 1.2; } } } return priv + toll;

candidates.name: Anticipatory Morning Metering
candidates.idea: Tolls ramp up steeply into the 8am buildup to preserve freeway and ramp headroom, then drop fast after 9am so queues flush without wasteful detours.

winner.name: Tiered Early Overload Toll
winner.idea: Tiered quadratic tolls spread planned load early by road type with peak and low-capacity multipliers plus a steep wall past 90 percent load to prevent queue spillover.

verdict: Adopted: Tiered Early Overload Toll beat the hand-tuned system by 3.36% on commuters it never saw.
lesson: Tiered tolls that rise early with congestion, charge extra for ramps, freeways, signals and low capacity roads during peaks, and add a steep overload penalty worked best and held up on unseen commuters, while broad spreading, fixed peak reserves, and elaborate ramp or morning metering schemes improved less. Next I would tune the peak windows and overload thresholds around that winning tiered structure and validate reliability across more demand patterns.
